logged.notes: lower back hurt a bit from doing rdl

thread.text:
Today: Squat 80kg × 5, 5, 5 again, same as 11-22, no knee complaint in the note — two sessions like that is exactly what the coach's call needed, so 82.5kg is earned for Sunday. RDL 80kg × 8, 8, 7, up from 7, 7, 7 last time — two sets at the top of the range, third dropped, and the note says the lower back felt it on this lift. Leg extension came in at 10kg × 10, 10, 10, down from the two 12s on 11-22; nothing in the log explains that drop except the back mention. Nordic curl ran instead of kneeling leg curl — bodyweight × 8, 8, 8, the first time it's in the log, so no trend to read yet. Seated calf raise and hanging leg raise didn't appear this time.

Heart rate: 50 minutes start to end, 93 avg, 65–134 bpm, most of it sitting in the 80s and 90s. It climbed to 110 around the 15-minute mark — likely the squat or RDL working sets — then settled back into the 80s–90s for the rest. That's in line with the week's other lifting sessions (48 min/93 avg, 54 min/90 avg, 69 min/97 avg), nothing unusual.

Sleep: 7h23 the night before, HRV 128 against the week's average of 118 — a good reading, no sign here that sleep is behind the back niggle. No normal yet to measure either number against (13 of 14 nights logged).

Question: was the lower back thing a mild tightness or something that changed how the RDL sets felt as you went? That decides whether 82.5kg is still the plan for the RDL or whether it's worth dropping to 75kg for a session first.

Next session: Sunday Lower — squat moves to 82.5kg for 3×3-5, knees still the guard. RDL stays at 80kg, 6–8, with the aim of all three sets at 8 before any jump — back permitting. Leg extension back toward 12s if the previous drop was just fatigue, not the back. Bring the calf raise and hanging leg raise back in, or log them if they happened off the books.
